Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BEAC direct operation/99.2% ownership of GIMACPAY, acts as overseer, settler, and operator through GIMAC.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 CEMAC/GIMACPAY case study, which confirms the regional central bank BEAC operates the GIMACPAY instant payment system through GIMAC (Groupement Interbancaire Monetique de l'Afrique Centrale), which BEAC majority-owns and for which it also acts as overseer and settler; GIMACPAY serves all CEMAC member states including CAR. Also checked beac.int, which confirms GIMAC's affiliation with BEAC but adds no further detail. Score of 5 (Direct Operation) is confirmed and is well supported, but it sits at the top of the variable's 0-5 scale, so flagging for human review per top-of-scale policy.
revised_comments: The regional central bank, Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC), directly operates the GIMACPAY instant payment system that serves the Central African Republic as a member of the CEMAC monetary union. GIMACPAY is run by GIMAC, an interbank grouping that BEAC majority-owns, with BEAC also acting as the scheme's overseer and settlement agent.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Low uptake inferred from banking <1%, mobile money growing but low penetration; no CAR-specific Findex data found.
revision_notes: The originally cited source (a general Wikipedia country overview) contains no financial-inclusion data and does not support the score. Fetched and read the World Bank Public Sector Digital Governance Project Appraisal Document (March 2022), which reports that only 13.7% of the adult population (9.7% of women) had access to a financial account as of around 2021, and CAR has one of the lowest mobile money agent densities in the CEMAC region (about 15 agents per 100,000 adults, concentrated in Bangui). Also read the Carnegie Endowment's 2023 report on digital finance in CAR, which corroborates low uptake of mobile money and digital wallets nationally. Both sources support active digital payment usage well below 20% of adults. Score of 1 confirmed and re-sourced.
revised_comments: Active use of digital payments among the adult population remains low. Around 14% of adults hold any financial account, whether at a bank or via mobile money, and agent networks for cashing in and out of mobile wallets remain thin outside the capital, Bangui. Active digital payment usage is well below 20% of the adult population.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Limited govt adoption via Patapaye but low activity ~20%.
revision_notes: The originally cited source was the generic World Bank homepage, not a specific document, and did not support the score. Fetched and read the World Bank Public Sector Digital Governance Project Appraisal Document (March 2022), which describes the Patapaye mobile-money civil servant salary pilot: only 2,500 of a targeted 7,000 civil servants had subscribed, and only around 20% of subscribers were active users, as of November 2021, against a national civil service far larger than the pilot's scope, and with pensions and most social transfers still paid conventionally. This confirms government-to-person digitisation remains well under 20% of total government payments. Score of 1 confirmed and re-sourced.
revised_comments: Digitisation of government payments remains limited. The flagship initiative, Patapaye, pays a subset of civil servants' salaries via mobile money in partnership with Orange and Ecobank, but take-up has been modest, with only a few thousand civil servants enrolled and roughly one-fifth of those active users. The great majority of government-to-person disbursements, including most salaries, pensions and social transfers, continue to be made through cash or conventional bank channels rather than the instant digital payment system.
